title: Democratic stagnation and declining rights are increasingly linked to conflict conditions and weakened institutional checks
source_unit: International IDEA, The Global State of Democracy 2026: Democracy in an Age of Conflict
geography: 173 countries assessed through the Global State of Democracy Indices, with regional comparisons and conflict analysis

denominator.unit: countries assessed in the Global State of Democracy Indices

countries_declining_any_indicator.unit: percent of assessed countries declining in at least one key democratic indicator between 2020 and 2025

decline_streak.unit: consecutive years in which more countries showed net democratic decline than improvement

assessment_categories.value: Representation, Rights, Rule of Law, and Participation

observations.method: International IDEA assessment using the Global State of Democracy Indices across four categories and 17 factors.
observations.uncertainty: Index components have different data sources, coverage, and temporal resolution; decline in one indicator does not establish uniform national democratic collapse or causal conflict effects.
observations.subgroup: Countries across regions and levels of democratic performance, with institutions and citizens represented through country-level indicators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stagnation or decline on an index can coexist with localized reforms, civic mobilization, or improvements in other democratic dimensions; global aggregates can hide divergent trajectories.

denominator.unit: countries assessed in the Global State of Democracy Indices

rule_of_law_low_band.unit: countries, or 41 percent of those assessed, in the low-performance band for Rule of Law

rule_of_law_declines.unit: countries, or 17 percent of those assessed, recording Rule of Law downturns

freedom_expression_declines.unit: countries, or 24 percent of those assessed, with declining Freedom of Expression

freedom_press_declines.unit: percent of assessed countries with declining Freedom of the Press

observations.method: International IDEA category and factor-level comparison of Rule of Law and Rights indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Performance bands and changes summarize multidimensional indicators; they do not measure every form of repression, informal power, or citizen experience and are not causal estimates of media or judicial effects.
observations.subgroup: Judiciaries, media, civil society, citizens, and countries experiencing changes in expression, press freedom, judicial independence, or access to justice.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rights and rule-of-law declines can be reversed through institutional reform and public mobilization; low performance in a category does not mean all rights are equally impaired.

denominator.unit: countries assessed in the Global State of Democracy Indices

credible_elections_declines.unit: countries, or 18 percent of those assessed, with deterioration in Credible Elections

effective_parliament_declines.unit: countries, or 19 percent of those assessed, with deterioration in Effective Parliament

representation_changes.value: 17 declines and 4 advances in the Representation category

observations.method: International IDEA analysis of representation factors including electoral credibility and legislative effectiveness.
observations.uncertainty: Country-level indicator changes do not show why elections or parliaments weakened, how citizens interpreted them, or whether formal institutions retained informal legitimacy.
observations.subgroup: Voters, electoral authorities, legislatures, political parties, and countries with changing electoral integrity or legislative oversight.
observations.counterinterpretation: Electoral and parliamentary deterioration can coexist with peaceful alternation, civic resistance, or institutional learning; representation scores do not measure every form of participation between elections.

denominator.unit: International IDEA comparative democracy-conflict analytical framework

democratic_recession.value: erosion in democratic governance is associated in the report with concern about domestic and international conflict

hybrid_regime_risk.value: countries with some democratic procedures but weak political competition or unenforceable rights are described as especially exposed to conflict

positive_counterexamples.value: political transitions and civil-society mobilization produced improvements in selected countries, though gains remain fragile

observations.method: International IDEA synthesis of democracy-index trends and comparative conflict analysis; the report examines associations rather than estimating a single causal effect.
observations.uncertainty: The relationship between democratic quality and conflict is historically and institutionally contingent; association does not establish that democratic decline causes a particular conflict or that democracy support prevents one.
observations.subgroup: Countries in democratic transition, partial democracies, autocracies, well-functioning democracies, civil society, and conflict-affected populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional weakness may be both cause and consequence of conflict, while inclusive reforms and civic mobilization can improve resilience even under severe security pressure.

related_sources.claim: International IDEA Global State of Democracy 2025 provides the prior-year comparative baseline.
The 2026 report's full publication provides the methodology, regional trends, and conflict analysis.

boundary: This record adds a comparative democracy-to-conflict route linking representation, rights, rule of law, participation, institutional checks, and violent conflict conditions. It uses country-level indices and report analysis, not respondent-level political attitudes, individual voting histories, causal conflict forecasts, or a single overall democracy score.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official International IDEA 2026 report page and launch findings were reviewed for the 173-country frame, 2020-2025 trends, Rule of Law and Rights indicators, Representation changes, and democracy-conflict findings.
